### Observed differences

- In the later window, each of A33, A34, A36, A37, A38, A39, A40 and A41 runs in essentially every trace (199 of 200), up from roughly 47–55 in 100 traces before; each occurs about once per case with almost no repetition in either window. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008]
- Before, these eight activities formed two mutually exclusive packages: A33/A34/A36/A37 appeared together in about 54 in 100 traces and A38–A41 together in about 46 in 100, while cross-package pairs such as A33 with A38 co-occurred in only about 1–4 of 200 traces. [REL017, REL020, REL024, REL030, REL039]
- In the later window, both packages run in the same case: all 16 cross-package pairs co-occur in about 99 in 100 traces (for example, A33 with A38 rises from about 1 in 100 to 99 in 100). [REL020, REL021, REL022, REL023, REL026, REL027, REL028, REL029, REL031, REL032, REL033, REL034, REL035, REL036, REL037, REL038]
- When both packages run, A33/A34/A36/A37 precede A38–A41 in about 96–98 in 100 later-window traces, while order within each package stays roughly balanced between the two directions in both windows. [REL020, REL023, REL026, REL029, REL031, REL034, REL036, REL038, REL017, REL042]
- A30 and A31 continue to frame the segment: A30 appears in every trace in both windows and precedes each of the eight in about 97–99 in 100 later-window traces (co-occurrence up from about 47–55 in 100), and each of the eight now precedes A31 in about 95–97 in 100. [REL001, REL003, REL005, REL008, REL009, REL013, REL016]
- Routing moved consistently: A30's outgoing transitions, previously spread over all eight activities (about 9–15% each), now go about 96% to A33/A34/A36/A37; A33/A34/A36/A37 drop their direct transitions to A31 (from about 20–27% to at most about 0.5%) and gain transitions to A38–A41 (about 3–8%). [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005]
- Positions and event gaps agree: A30 and A33/A34/A36/A37 moved earlier in the trace (mean relative position from about 0.73–0.74 to about 0.59–0.65), A38–A41 moved slightly later (to about 0.76–0.77), and the event gap from A30 to A38–A41 and from A33/A34/A36/A37 to A31 falls into the largest measured bucket (5+ events) in about 97–98 in 100 later-window observations. [POS001, POS002, POS005, POS006, POS009, LAG002, LAG005, LAG006, LAG012, LAG016]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the segment between A30 and A31, which before executed either the A33/A34/A36/A37 package (about 54 in 100 cases) or the A38–A41 package (about 46 in 100), now executes both packages back to back in nearly every case — A30 first, then A33/A34/A36/A37 in no fixed internal order, then A38–A41 likewise, then A31. [REL020, REL035, REL001, REL016, DIR001]

The judgement rests on direct relational evidence rather than frequency shifts alone: cross-package co-occurrence rose from about 1–4 of 200 traces to about 99 in 100 with a stable package order, and the routing changes (A30 now feeds almost only the first package, which now feeds the second and no longer A31 directly) plus the position and gap shifts all point the same way. The many items collapse into about four distinct behavioural differences — clearly more than the roughly 1 expected by chance at these thresholds — and the key relations are measured on all 200 traces per window. [REL020, REL027, DIR001, DIR003, LAG006, POS002]

An important competing explanation remains: the both-packages behaviour may have existed before as a rare variant (about 1–2 in 100 traces) that the later window simply selects almost exclusively; with 200-trace samples, such a wholesale switch in variant frequencies cannot be distinguished from a modified process definition. In addition, within-package order is roughly balanced in both windows, so each package's internal structure stays undetermined, and a few lag profiles rest on only 1–3 observations and were not relied on. [REL020, REL017, LAG001, LAG007]
